description: Design system regulations for iOS applications based on Apple Human Interface Guidelines, App Store Review Guidelines, and WCAG accessibility standards.

references.name: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
references.description: Apple's comprehensive design guidance for all Apple platforms.

references.name: Apple Accessibility Guidelines
references.description: Apple's accessibility programming and design resources.

references.name: WCAG 2.1
references.description: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines used as baseline for mobile accessibility.

references.name: App Store Review Guidelines
references.description: Guidelines for app submission and approval on the App Store.

regulations.title: Dynamic Type Support
regulations.description: All text elements must support Dynamic Type to respect user font size preferences across the system.

rules.requirement: Body text must use at minimum the system 'body' text style (17pt at default scale) or equivalent.
rules.rationale: The body text style is the baseline readable size on iOS devices.

rules.requirement: All text must scale with Dynamic Type using UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:) or the equivalent SwiftUI .font() modifier with system text styles.
rules.rationale: Users who configure larger text sizes expect all apps to respect their preference.

rules.requirement: UI elements that cannot scale with Dynamic Type (e.g., tab bar labels, navigation bar titles) must support the Large Content Viewer accessibility feature.
rules.rationale: The Large Content Viewer provides a zoomed preview for elements that can't grow.

rules.requirement: Text containers must gracefully handle larger text sizes by wrapping, scrolling, or expanding. Text must never be clipped without providing access to the full content.
rules.rationale: Clipped text at larger Dynamic Type sizes makes content inaccessible.

regulations.title: Color and Appearance
regulations.description: Applications must implement a thoughtful color system that works across light and dark modes and meets accessibility requirements.

rules.requirement: Text and essential icons must meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA contrast ratios: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt+ or 14pt+ bold).
rules.rationale: Sufficient contrast is required for readability in varied lighting conditions.

rules.requirement: Applications must provide a full Dark Mode implementation using semantic/adaptive colors from the system palette or Asset Catalog named colors.
rules.rationale: Dark Mode is an expected iOS feature; apps without it appear broken in dark environments.

rules.requirement: Applications should prefer system-provided semantic colors (e.g., .label, .secondaryLabel, .systemBackground) which automatically adapt to appearance modes and accessibility settings.
rules.rationale: System colors automatically handle dark mode, high contrast, and reduce transparency settings.

rules.requirement: Color must not be the sole means of conveying meaning. Additional indicators such as shapes, icons, patterns, or text must supplement color-coded information.
rules.rationale: Color-blind users cannot distinguish information conveyed by color alone.

rules.requirement: Applications must support the 'Increase Contrast' accessibility setting by providing high-contrast color variants in the Asset Catalog.
rules.rationale: Users with low vision may enable Increase Contrast for better visibility.

regulations.title: Layout and Spacing
regulations.description: Applications must use iOS layout system conventions to ensure consistent spacing across all device sizes and orientations.

rules.requirement: All interactive elements must have a minimum tap target of 44x44 points.
rules.rationale: Apple's HIG specifies 44pt as the minimum comfortable tap target size.

rules.requirement: Content must be positioned within the Safe Area to avoid being obscured by the notch, Dynamic Island, home indicator, or rounded corners.
rules.rationale: Ignoring Safe Areas causes content to be hidden behind hardware features.

rules.requirement: Content must use the system layout margins (at least 16pt on compact width, 20pt on regular width) for consistent edge spacing.
rules.rationale: System layout margins ensure content is well-inset and consistent with the platform.

rules.requirement: Applications must support all multitasking modes on iPad including Split View, Slide Over, and Stage Manager by using adaptive layouts.
rules.rationale: iPad users expect apps to work seamlessly in multitasking configurations.

regulations.title: Accessibility Compliance
regulations.description: Applications must be fully accessible using VoiceOver, Switch Control, and other iOS assistive technologies.

rules.requirement: All interactive elements and meaningful images must have descriptive accessibilityLabel values. Decorative images must be marked as not accessible.
rules.rationale: VoiceOver reads accessibility labels aloud; missing labels render the app unusable.

rules.requirement: Elements must have correct accessibilityTraits (button, header, link, image, etc.) so assistive technologies convey the element's role properly.
rules.rationale: Correct traits help VoiceOver users understand what an element does.

rules.requirement: Applications must respect the 'Reduce Motion' accessibility preference by replacing complex animations with simple dissolve transitions or removing them entirely.
rules.rationale: Motion can cause nausea or discomfort for users with vestibular disorders.

rules.requirement: When content changes (navigation, modals, alerts), accessibility focus must be moved to the new content so VoiceOver users are aware of the change.
rules.rationale: Without focus management, VoiceOver users may not realize the screen has changed.

rules.requirement: Complex gestures (swipe-to-delete, long press menus) must provide accessible alternatives via accessibilityCustomActions or standard system gestures.
rules.rationale: Users of Switch Control and VoiceOver cannot perform custom gestures.

regulations.title: Component Standards
regulations.description: UI components must follow Human Interface Guidelines patterns for consistent, intuitive user experiences.

rules.requirement: Applications must use UINavigationController (push/pop) for hierarchical navigation and UITabBarController for flat, top-level navigation between sections.
rules.rationale: Standard navigation patterns are familiar to iOS users and integrate with system gestures.

rules.requirement: Action Sheets must be used for presenting a set of alternatives related to an action the user initiated. Action Sheets must include a cancel option.
rules.rationale: Action Sheets are the iOS convention for contextual choices and must be dismissible.

rules.requirement: Alerts must be reserved for important information requiring acknowledgment or a critical decision. Alerts must have concise titles and offer clear action buttons.
rules.rationale: Excessive alerts train users to dismiss them without reading, reducing their effectiveness.

rules.requirement: Scrollable lists of updatable content should implement the standard UIRefreshControl pull-to-refresh pattern.
rules.rationale: Pull-to-refresh is a deeply ingrained iOS gesture that users expect for refreshing content.

regulations.title: Navigation and Gestures
regulations.description: Navigation must follow iOS platform conventions and support standard system gestures.

rules.requirement: Applications using navigation controllers must not disable the interactive edge-swipe-back gesture. Custom gesture recognizers must not conflict with it.
rules.rationale: The swipe-back gesture is fundamental to iOS navigation; disabling it confuses users.

rules.requirement: Navigation bars must include a visible back button with the previous screen's title. Custom back buttons must maintain the chevron icon and back navigation behavior.
rules.rationale: The back button is the primary visual indicator of navigational hierarchy.

rules.requirement: The tab bar must remain visible during navigation within each tab's hierarchy unless the user enters a focused, immersive experience.
rules.rationale: Hiding the tab bar unexpectedly disorients users within the app's structure.

regulations.title: Animation and Motion
regulations.description: Animations must feel fluid and purposeful, adhering to iOS motion principles.

rules.requirement: Animations should use spring-based timing curves for natural-feeling motion. Linear and ease-in-out curves should be used sparingly.
rules.rationale: Spring animations are the signature motion style of iOS and feel natural.

rules.requirement: Standard UI transitions should be between 250ms and 450ms. Micro-interactions should be 100ms to 200ms.
rules.rationale: iOS animations feel fast and responsive within these ranges.

rules.requirement: When Reduce Motion is enabled, replace slide transitions with cross-dissolves and disable parallax, bouncing, and scaling animations.
rules.rationale: Compliance with Reduce Motion is essential for users with vestibular conditions.

regulations.title: Feedback and Communication
regulations.description: Applications must provide clear, consistent feedback using iOS platform patterns.

rules.requirement: Applications must use the UIFeedbackGenerator APIs for haptic feedback on supported devices. Impact, notification, and selection feedback types must match the context of the interaction.
rules.rationale: Appropriate haptics enhance the tactile quality of the experience on iOS.

rules.requirement: Errors must be presented in context (inline near the affected element) rather than as top-level alerts whenever possible. Error messages must describe the problem and offer a recovery path.
rules.rationale: Inline errors reduce disruption and help users understand what to fix.

rules.requirement: Loading states must use the system UIActivityIndicatorView for indeterminate progress or UIProgressView for determinate progress. Skeleton screens are preferred for content loading.
rules.rationale: Consistent loading indicators set user expectations about wait times.

regulations.title: Privacy and Data Handling
regulations.description: Applications must follow Apple's privacy principles and App Store requirements for user data handling.

rules.requirement: Applications must accurately declare all data collection and usage in the App Store privacy nutrition labels.
rules.rationale: Inaccurate privacy labels can result in App Store rejection and erode user trust.

rules.requirement: Permission requests (camera, location, notifications) must include a clear, specific purpose string explaining why the permission is needed at the moment it is requested.
rules.rationale: Contextual, just-in-time permission requests have higher grant rates and are required by Apple.

rules.requirement: Applications that track users across other apps or websites must present the ATT (App Tracking Transparency) prompt before collecting any tracking data.
rules.rationale: ATT is mandatory as of iOS 14.5 and failure to comply results in App Store rejection.

regulations.title: Icon and Image Standards
regulations.description: Icons and images must follow Apple's design guidelines for clarity and platform consistency.

rules.requirement: Applications should use SF Symbols for system-style icons to ensure consistency with the platform and automatic support for Dynamic Type, weight, and accessibility features.
rules.rationale: SF Symbols scale with text, support multiple weights, and are familiar to iOS users.

rules.requirement: Application icons must be provided as a single 1024x1024 point PNG image. The icon must not contain transparency or rounded corners (the system applies the mask).
rules.rationale: The system derives all icon sizes from the single source image.

rules.requirement: All raster images must be provided at @1x, @2x, and @3x resolutions or as vector (PDF/SVG) assets to support all device display scales.
rules.rationale: Missing resolution variants result in blurry images on higher-density screens.
